basis: Congenital malformation of the ear.
Congenital duplication and fusion of digits, with abnormal phalanges.
Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma arising in skin.
Defined reproductive abnormalities include testicular maldevelopment, cryptorchidism, hypospadias, infertility and germ-cell cancer; endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Alopecia universalis and severe intellectual disability define the syndrome.
Persistent central vestibular motion-perception dysfunction; peripheral ear damage is not established, and ocular findings are occasional (5-29%).
Benign neoplasm located in the nasopharynx, an upper-airway structure.
Cancer arising in lower gingiva; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Anomalous pulmonary artery origin and course; clinically significant tracheobronchial compression or stenosis occurs commonly (roughly half or more).
Umbrella of mineral metabolism and transport disorders; no additional organ is consistently damaged across its subtypes.
Immunodeficiency with absent circulating B cells; eczematoid dermatitis affects 2/6 (~33%). Thrombocytopenia also occurs in 2/6; hearing loss is below threshold.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy; muscle atrophy affects 80-99%, with structural hand/finger contractures in 30-79%.
Hereditary motor neuronopathy; fixed pes cavus and thenar muscle atrophy occur in 4/4 patients, with peroneal atrophy in 3/4.
Defined as a nervous system disorder with pain as a major feature; pain alone does not establish damage to other organs.
Severe bladder voiding dysfunction defines the syndrome; reflux and hydronephrosis are frequent. Recurrent UTIs are separate infections; constipation alone is insufficient.
Neurodevelopmental impairment, seizures and CNS malformations define disease. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; feeding difficulty does not establish GI damage.
Selective immunoglobulin production deficiency; blood-cell depletion and common direct organ damage are not established across this umbrella.
Neuronal lipid-storage disease with epilepsy and cognitive decline; supplied phenotypes report progressive visual loss and retinal/optic dysfunction in 30-79%.
Dysraphic fatty infiltration of the filum terminale; associated extraspinal abnormalities are not established as common.
Beta-amino-acid metabolic accumulation with explicitly described neurotoxicity, encephalopathy and convulsions.
Skeletal dysplasia, retinal degeneration and neurodevelopmental/CNS abnormalities define syndrome; sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 4/4 (100%), filling the fourth axis.
Developmental malformation of cochlear and vestibular ear structures.
Congenital restrictive ophthalmoplegia with extraocular muscle fibrosis and defining ulnar hand, digit and carpal malformations.
Cleft lips, gingival/labial mucosal fusion and abnormal dentition define an oral malformation; nonspecific facial morphology does not establish additional skeletal damage.
Isolated microphthalmia with retinal degeneration, foveoschisis and impaired vision; manifestations remain within the ocular axis.
